events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.74 (model confidence 0.66)
events.body:
RydeTAXI is metered, so extra kilometres enter the fare; each off-route segment in F3 and F4 is reviewed separately under RD-1 and refunded at this trip's per-km rate unless exempt [F3][F4][F5][RD-1][RD-2].

Segment F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km): the only rider message before it is F10 at 18:43, “Sure, your call.”, answering the driver's F9 question “ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?”. The acceptance is worded as a general choice of way (“your call”), and the segment's whole purpose is to get the rider to Orchard Road around the jam on the Bukit Timah Expressway, corroborated by the congestion record [F9][F10][F13]. A general route authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination, and it was given before the segment began, so F3 is exempt [F10][F9][RD-5].

The trace settles the RD-4 screen: no traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch was reported before the detour, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F15][RD-4].

Segment F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km): this begins 20 minutes after the rider's only message, and the rider's complaint states he agreed only to the first detour and that the driver went off route a second time without asking. Nothing in the complete, fully timestamped chat record (2 messages) shows any rider message before 19:03:25 agreeing to a second diversion [F11][F10]. The driver's explanation of a GPS reroute appears only in his post-trip statement, which is not rider consent [F12][RD-5]. No rider-requested stop was measured in either segment, so RD-3(a) is not engaged for F4 [F9][F10][F4][RD-3].

Amount: the unexempt segment F4 added 4.78 km; rate = $43.64 ÷ 30.95 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8]. 4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.7398 → $6.74 [F4][F5][RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so no account flag attaches [F18][RD-6].
